verdict.line: You lose if you trade into his Fury-capped all-in at level 3-5; you win if you survive that window and drag it to items, since the head-to-head sits at 50.4% over 685 games despite Renekton owning lane and solo-kill priority.

brief.thesis: Renekton's Fury bar is the whole matchup: at 100 Fury his Q, W, and E all empower, turning a normal trade into a stun-into-double-dash-into-execute-range burst that explains his lane and solo-kill edge. Sett has no way to out-trade that burst directly, but Haymaker's missing-health scaling and Facebreaker's stun let you survive the spike and win every fight that happens after his Fury dumps.

theirWindow.what: Do not walk up for a trade here. His empowered W (Ruthless Predator) stuns longer and hits in a cone, and it chains into empowered E (Slice and Dice) for a second dash-reset — that combo is the actual source of his solo-kill lead, so hold Haymaker's shield up or just give ground until it's spent.

yourWindow.when: After his empowered combo whiffs or lands
yourWindow.what: His Fury resets to near zero and Slice and Dice goes on a real cooldown (9-14s early). Walk him down immediately, land E (Facebreaker) to pull and stun, then follow with W and autos — this is the only window where you out-damage him in a straight fight.

start.why: It's the dominant start at 52.3% over 665 games and 79.6% pick — the extra sustain and damage let you hold trades until his empowered burst is spent instead of losing the poke war outright.

boots.why: 50.6% over 601 games and the clear majority pick (76.6%) — Renekton's damage is almost entirely auto-attacks plus his empowered Cull the Meek autos, and flat armor per hit cuts both.

core.why: Highest-sample core path opener; the active gives you the gap-close to punish him the moment his Fury combo is on cooldown.
Shows up in every top core path here — the shield and bonus health directly counter his burst windows.

This exact path (Stridebreaker > Overlord's Bloodmail > Sterak's Gage) posts 61.2% over 49 games, the best measured winrate of any core sequence, and the tenacity/shield helps you survive his stun-chain all-ins specifically.

situational.when: he's building armor or you need the shred to actually kill him before his Fury regenerates
the game goes long and you need ability haste to reset Facebreaker faster than he resets Fury
he's stacking health items and you need the percent-health damage to keep dueling him late

runes.keystoneWhy: You need the stacking sustain to win extended fights after his burst window closes, since you can't out-trade the initial empowered combo — Conqueror's healing is what lets the post-Fury duel actually favor you.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is run in 92.1% of games at 50.7% winrate — Ignite both threatens the execute after you survive his all-in and cuts the healing off his empowered Cull the Meek so his sustain in the trade window doesn't compound.

playing.title: Bank W for his Fury spike
playing.detail: Once his Fury bar approaches full around level 3, don't be mid-animation on a trade — have Haymaker's shield ready to absorb the empowered Ruthless Predator stun-and-damage instead of eating it raw.

playing.title: Never trade into a loaded dash
playing.detail: Empowered Slice and Dice hits twice and repositions him — walking up when he has both Fury and E up is how you feed the solo-kill stat directly.

playing.title: Punish the post-combo cooldown
playing.detail: After his all-in lands or misses, Slice and Dice is down for 9-14 seconds early. Close the gap with Facebreaker's pull-stun immediately and commit the fight.

playing.title: Play around waves before level 6
playing.detail: Don't shove into range where he can engage for free during the 3-5 window; let the wave push to you so you can disengage into minions if his Fury is up.

playing.title: Use Haymaker as a comeback tool
playing.detail: Its shield and damage scale up the lower your own health is, so a fight that starts bad for you can flip once you dip below half — don't panic-back, threaten the return trade instead.

playing.title: Itemize Cleaver if he snowballs
playing.detail: If he gets ahead off an early solo kill, swap the Sterak's slot for Black Cleaver — the armor shred and grievous wounds interaction claw back the duel faster than raw HP does.

playing.title: Force fights after Stridebreaker
playing.detail: From level 11 on, your build's sustained fighting stats catch up to his flat Fury burst — start initiating with E into R rather than waiting for him to engage.

brief.patchCaveat: Winrates, pick rates, sample sizes, item paths, runes, boots, and summoner spells above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning — Fury timing, dash windows, trade patterns — is my own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Keep an eye out on Renekton’s Fury before fighting him. Use [W] when he tries using his reinforced skill to gain the upper hand in combat.
